status: prototype; no production certification or universal speed claim

methodology.query_timing: warm in-process parse, execute, materialize; Rust direct API versus Python native bindings; different boundary costs
methodology.execution_order: Kestrel memory, Kestrel durable/reopened, Kestrel Python pipe, then each SQLite/DuckDB query; shared live machine, no affinity
limitations: ingestion methods differ; load times are diagnostic, not fair ingestion rankings
Kestrel stores 128-bit prefix sums: 3x logical integer data size
general scan and grouping cases included; competitors support far more SQL

sqlite_manual_prefix_baseline.maintenance: prebuilt prefix table; an application or trigger must maintain it on future ordered appends
sqlite_manual_prefix_baseline.limits: unique ordered timestamp dataset; 64-bit-safe sums; extra schema and rewritten queries

sqlite_manual_prefix.rewritten_sql:
WITH bounds AS (
            SELECT COALESCE((SELECT n FROM cumulative WHERE ts < 1000000 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1),0) AS hn,
            COALESCE((SELECT total FROM cumulative WHERE ts < 1000000 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1),0) AS hs,
            COALESCE((SELECT n FROM cumulative WHERE ts < 0 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1),0) AS ln,
            COALESCE((SELECT total FROM cumulative WHERE ts < 0 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1),0) AS ls)
            SELECT hn-ln, CASE WHEN hn>ln THEN hs-ls END, CASE WHEN hn>ln THEN 1.0*(hs-ls)/(hn-ln) END FROM bounds
